1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
5	\label{sec:setup}
6	
7	We study lead-lag analysis design considerations in iterative training collapse using Pythia-410M~\cite{biderman2023pythia} (410M parameters, decoder-only), with cross-architecture validation on GPT-2-medium (345M) and three additional families (\S\ref{sec:generalization}).
8	Training data is drawn from WikiText-103~\cite{merity2017pointer} following the replace paradigm of~\citet{shumailov2024curse}: each generation fine-tunes on a mixture of $\alpha$ synthetic and $(1{-}\alpha)$ real data, generates 5{,}000 replacement samples, and fully replaces the synthetic pool (hyperparameters in Appendix~\ref{app:training_details}; notation in Appendix~\ref{app:background}).
9	We run $T{=}10$ generations across 13 contamination levels ($\alpha \in \{0.00, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.40, 0.45, 0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.75, 1.00\}$, including null control) with multi-seed replication (4 seeds at $\alpha{=}1.0$; 3 at primary levels).
10	
11	We track two \emph{canary metrics}---token entropy and ECE---and three \emph{downstream metrics}: distinct-1, distinct-2~\cite{li2016diversity}, and perplexity (distinct-3: Appendix~\ref{app:distinct3}).
12	All hypothesis tests apply BH-FDR correction at $q{=}0.05$; PermG uses 5{,}000 permutations on first-differenced series~\cite{shojaie2022granger} with maximum lag~5 (window sensitivity: Appendix~\ref{app:window_sensitivity}).
13	
14	
15	\subsection{Sharp Detection Onset}
16	\label{sec:regime}
17	
18	Diversity collapse occurs at every contamination level: distinct-1 declines by $14.1\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.0$ (fine-tuning drift) and by $40.3{\pm}0.3\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.25$ (3-seed mean).
19	Despite this ubiquitous degradation, Granger detectability is sharply regime-dependent.
20	The onset we report reflects PermG's statistical power curve crossing the detection threshold at a critical contamination level, not the emergence of a new physical signal; this interpretation is confirmed by sub-threshold $p$-values at $\alpha{=}0.45$ (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
21	Permutation Granger (PermG) tests find 0/8 canary$\to$downstream pairs FDR-significant from $\alpha{=}0.00$ through $\alpha{=}0.45$, then jump to 6/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ uniformly across all 3~fp32 seeds.
22	This transition is striking because cumulative synthetic fraction barely changes across the boundary: $C = 1{-}(1{-}\alpha)^{10}$ yields $99.75\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.45$ versus $99.90\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.50$, a difference of 0.15 percentage points, yet detection jumps from null to reliable.
23	Sigmoid regression on the 13-point $T{=}10$ grid yields $\alpha_c = 0.483 \pm 0.006$ ($R^2 = 0.969$); dense $\alpha$ sampling (17~values) constrains the onset steepness to $k{=}15.7$ (95\% CI $[9.4, 28.2]$), a steep but finite-width sigmoid (Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response}).
24	This single-$T$ estimate is consistent with the cross-$T$ validated model (\S\ref{sec:theory}), which predicts how the detection boundary shifts with observation length ($\gamma{=}2.08$).
25	The transition is not a literal step function ($\Delta\mathrm{AIC}{=}-110$ favoring sigmoid; Appendix~\ref{app:sigmoid_shape}), but its steepness (${\approx}3{\times}$ smooth-model predictions; \S\ref{sec:theory}) exceeds what PermG power curves alone produce.
26	At $T{=}10$, PermG power is ${\approx}37\%$ (Appendix~\ref{app:power_sim}), partly amplifying the $0/8{\to}6/8$ sharpness; however, onset steepness ($k{=}15.7$, ${\approx}3{\times}$ smooth predictions) and cross-seed consistency (3/3 seeds: $0/8{\to}6/8$ at $\alpha{=}0.48{\to}0.50$) argue for a genuine, power-modulated transition.
27	A Fisher exact test corroborates the categorical jump: 0/64 pairs FDR-significant at $\alpha \leq 0.45$ versus 18/32 at $\alpha \geq 0.50$ ($p = 3.45 \times 10^{-11}$); sub-threshold $p$-values at $\alpha{=}0.45$ ($p_{\mathrm{fdr}} = 0.059$--$0.091$) are consistent with proximity to the power boundary (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
28	A systematic robustness analysis (1{,}160 configurations) confirms specification-invariance of the onset.
29	
30	\paragraph{Canary scoping.}
31	First-differencing scopes the canary claim precisely.
32	Canary$\to$diversity pairs retain unanimous FDR significance after first-differencing ($24/24 \to 24/24$ across 4~seeds at $\alpha{=}1.0$, 6 pairs per seed), while canary$\to$perplexity collapses entirely ($F \approx 0$, $p = 0.99$): the apparent perplexity association is a shared-trend artifact.
33	All canary claims are therefore scoped to diversity metrics only.
34	This scoping reflects a genuine temporal structure difference, not selective power loss from differencing: $|r|$ retention is ${\geq}95\%$ for both channels, but canary$\to$diversity correlations peak at lagged offsets (81\% at lag${<}0$, median${=}-1$) while canary$\to$perplexity correlations are contemporaneous (50\% at lag${=}0$), producing $20$--$28{\times}$ lower Granger $F$ for perplexity (Appendix~\ref{app:channel_effect_size}; perplexity $n{=}8$, limited sample).
35	At $\alpha{=}1.0$, all 24 canary$\to$diversity pairs (6 per seed $\times$ 4~seeds; mauve excluded) reach FDR significance in the forward direction with 0/24 reverse; directional asymmetry is robust across all WikiText conditions.
36	Independent of the Granger test, the degradation cascade confirms temporal precedence: entropy onset at generation~1 precedes distinct-$n$ onset at generation~2 in 16/18 WikiText conditions (Kendall $\tau{=}0.337$; \S\ref{sec:cascade}, Appendix~\ref{app:moment_cascade}), with supporting change-point analysis (Appendix~\ref{app:change_point}).
37	The canary mechanism also exhibits a blind spot: at $\alpha{=}0.10$, distinct-1 has already dropped by $39.6\%$, yet token entropy is indistinguishable from the null ($-5.3\%$ versus $-4.6{\pm}0.4\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.0$).
38	The gen-1 entropy deviation spans three orders of magnitude across the $\alpha$ range: $0.5\sigma$ at $\alpha{=}0.10$ to $60\sigma$ at $\alpha{=}0.75$ (relative to null variability), explaining why the blind zone persists despite increasing contamination.\footnote{Seed~43 at $\alpha{=}0.10$ shows 3/8 versus 0/8 for seed~42; no other sub-threshold level exhibits seed-dependent detection.}
39	Below $\alpha_c$ at $T{=}10$, diversity collapse proceeds without any detectable Granger-precedence signal in the canary metrics, though Gaussian MI remains positive (Appendix~\ref{app:mi_analysis}).
40	
41	\begin{figure*}[t]
42	\centering
43	\includegraphics[width=0.65\textwidth]{figures/metric_trajectory.pdf}
44	\caption{Metric trajectories at $\alpha{=}1.0$ (Pythia-410M, 4~seeds). Token entropy drops at generation~1; distinct-1 declines from generations~2--3, with a consistent one-generation canary lead across all four seeds (shaded: inter-seed range). This pattern corresponds to 24/24 forward and 0/24 reverse FDR-significant canary$\to$diversity pairs (6 per seed, mauve excluded).}
45	\label{fig:metric_trajectory}
46	\end{figure*}
47	
48	
49	\subsection{Dose-Response and Detection Regimes}
50	\label{sec:dose_response}
51	
52	\begin{figure}[t]
53	\centering
54	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_dose_response.pdf}
55	\caption{PermG dose-response profile (Pythia-410M, $T{=}10$, fp32). Sigmoid fit (shaded 95\% CI) yields $\alpha_c{=}0.483$. Four regimes: blind ($\alpha{\leq}0.45$, 0/8), onset ($\alpha{\approx}0.50$, 6/8), sync-dip ($\alpha{=}0.60$, 0/8), and detection ($\alpha{\geq}0.75$).}
56	\label{fig:dose_response}
57	\end{figure}
58	
59	The PermG dose-response profile (Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response}; full per-method table in Appendix~\ref{app:dose_response}) reveals four detection regimes: \emph{blind} ($\alpha \leq 0.45$, 0/8 FDR-significant pairs), \emph{onset} ($\alpha \approx 0.50$, 6/8), \emph{non-monotonic dip} ($\alpha \approx 0.60$, 0/8), and \emph{detection} ($\alpha{\geq}0.75$, 6/8 across 4~seeds at $\alpha{=}1.0$).
60	At $\alpha{=}0.55$, PermG returns 0/8 FDR-significant pairs despite marginal $p$-values ($p_{\mathrm{fdr}}{=}0.062$--$0.092$); differenced cross-correlation detects 8/8 bidirectionally at this level, confirming that a lead-lag signal exists but falls below PermG's directional detection threshold.
61	At $\alpha{=}0.60$, PermG returns $0/8$ at $T{\leq}20$ but recovers to $5/8$ at $T{=}25$, confirming a transient dip that $\sqrt{T}$ power eventually overcomes (Appendix~\ref{app:t20_comparison}).
62	
63	Method choice is itself a major source of variability: at $\alpha{=}1.0$, direction-checked forward significance spans 0\% to 75\% (Table~\ref{tab:method_comparison}), with $\kappa{=}0.185$; a specification curve (18~variants; Appendix~\ref{app:spec_curve}) confirms onset invariance.
64	Task degradation corroborates: perplexity jumps $+31\%$ between $\alpha{=}0.50$ and $0.52$ (Appendix~\ref{app:task_degradation}).
65	
66	
67	\begin{table}[t]
68	\centering
69	\small
70	\caption{Forward-direction FDR significance rates (\%) across contamination levels (Pythia-410M, seed~42, fp32; $3\sigma$ threshold calibration, lag-direction filtering for cross-correlation methods). Each cell: fraction of 8 validated pairs at BH-corrected significance ($q{=}0.05$). PermG achieves the lowest null-control FPR among directional methods (seed-42: 0/8; pooled 6-seed: 11.1\%) with consistent detection at $\alpha \geq 0.50$.}
71	\label{tab:method_comparison}
72	\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
73	\begin{tabular}{lcccccc}
74	\toprule
75	Method & $\alpha{=}0.0$ & $\alpha{=}0.25$ & $\alpha{=}0.50$ & $\alpha{=}0.75$ & $\alpha{=}1.0$ & FPR$_\text{null}$ \\
76	\midrule
77	Naive XCorr          & 75   & 62.5 & 62.5 & 0    & 0    & 75  \\
78	Diff.\ XCorr         & 0    & 25   & 12.5 & 0    & 0    & 0   \\
79	Threshold ($3\sigma$) & 37.5 & 62.5 & 100  & 100  & 25   & 37.5 \\
80	Perm.\ Granger       & \textbf{0}    & \textbf{0}    & \textbf{75}   & \textbf{75}   & \textbf{75}   & \textbf{0}   \\
81	Toda--Yamamoto$^\S$  & 12.5 & 37.5 & 50   & 100  & 12.5 & 12.5 \\
82	\bottomrule
83	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\footnotesize $^\S$TY directional assignment under verification; row retained for completeness.} \\
84	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\footnotesize Pooled FPR (3 seeds, cluster-bootstrap 95\% CI): \S\ref{sec:mmct}.} \\
85	\end{tabular}}
86	\end{table}
87	
88	
89	\subsection{Detection Boundary Left-Shift}
90	\label{sec:t20}
91	
92	The detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$ decreases monotonically: $\alpha_c(5){\geq}1.0$, $\alpha_c(10){=}0.487$, consistent with $T^{-2.08}$ power scaling (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
93	The $\alpha{=}0.45$ column traces the sharpest validation: $0/8$ at $T{\leq}10$, $6/8$ at $T{=}15$ (dual-seed), $5/8$ at $T{=}20$, $6/8$ at $T{=}25$.
94	The systematic 2/8 gap reflects MAUVE floor saturation ($\mu{=}0.029$, SNR $4.68$ vs diversity $6.40$--$8.20$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
95	Cross-seed replication shows PermG within ${\pm}1$, though boundary cells exhibit sensitivity: $[0, 6]/8$ at ($T{=}10$, $\alpha{=}0.50$); $[0, 3]/8$ at ($T{=}20$, $\alpha{=}0.60$).
96	Minimum $T$ for 80\% power at $\alpha{=}0.50$ is approximately $T{=}30$ (extrapolated from simulation; Appendix~\ref{app:power_sim}).
97	The $\alpha{=}0.60$ dip dissolves by $T{=}25$ ($5/8$), validating $\sqrt{T}$ power scaling; predict-then-verify (commit \texttt{bad72cc}) yields 2/4 boundary predictions within CI (Appendix~\ref{app:t20_prediction_timeline}).
98	
99	
100	\subsection{Cross-Architecture Validation}
101	\label{sec:generalization}
102	
103	We evaluate PermG across 15 model-seed combinations spanning five families, scales 345M--6.9B, and two domains (Table~\ref{tab:generalization}).
104	PermG reaches ${\geq}6/8$ in 11/15 conditions where entropy declines monotonically before diversity; C4 yields strongest detection (Pythia-1.4B: 2/8 WikiText $\to$ 8/8 C4).
105	Non-confirming conditions span precision sensitivity (GPT-2 bf16: 0/8 vs fp32: 6/8), bidirectional confounding (GPT-2 s43), seed dependence (Pythia-1.4B: s42 2/8, s43 6/8), and entropy decoupling (SmolLM3-3B: 3/8, entropy 0/4).
106	
107	\begin{table}[t]
108	\centering
109	\small
110	\caption{Cross-architecture PermG forward detection ($\alpha{=}1.0$, 15 model-seed combinations across five families and two domains).}
111	\label{tab:generalization}
112	\begin{tabular}{lrcl}
113	\toprule
114	Model & Params & Domain & PermG fwd \\
115	\midrule
116	Pythia-410M    & 410M & Wiki & \textbf{6/8} \\
117	Pythia-1.4B    & 1.4B & Wiki & 2--6/8$^\dagger$ \\
118	Pythia-6.9B    & 6.9B & Wiki & \textbf{7/8}$^*$ \\
119	GPT-2-medium   & 345M & Wiki & \textbf{6/8}$^\S$ \\
120	OPT-1.3B       & 1.3B & Wiki & \textbf{6/8} \\
121	Qwen3.5-0.8B   & 0.8B & Wiki & \textbf{8/8} \\
122	SmolLM3-3B     & 3.0B & Wiki & 3/8$^\ddagger$ \\
123	Padding-410M   & 410M & Wiki & \textbf{6/8} \\
124	\addlinespace
125	Pythia-1B      & 1.0B & C4   & \textbf{8/8} \\
126	Pythia-1.4B    & 1.4B & C4   & \textbf{8/8} \\
127	\bottomrule
128	\multicolumn{4}{l}{\footnotesize $^\dagger$Seed-dep.\ (s42: 2/8, s43: 6/8); 8-pair incl.\ MAUVE} \\
129	\multicolumn{4}{l}{\footnotesize \phantom{$^\dagger$}(floor ${\sim}0.033$ at 1.4B; 6-pair in Table~\ref{tab:14b_phase}). $^*$bf16. $^\ddagger$ECE-only (ent.\ 0/4).} \\
130	\multicolumn{4}{l}{\footnotesize $^\S$s42 fp32: 6/8 fwd, 0 rev; s43: 6/8 both; bf16: 0/8.} \\
131	\multicolumn{4}{l}{\footnotesize 2 seeds each for Pythia-410M/1.4B, GPT-2, OPT, Pythia-1B C4.} \\
132	\end{tabular}
133	\end{table}
134	
135	
136	\subsection{Canary-Based Intervention (Proof of Concept)}
137	\label{sec:intervention}
138	
139	As an illustrative proof-of-concept under favorable conditions ($\alpha{=}1.0$, full replacement), we implement predictive cessation: training switches to pure real data when token entropy drops ${>}15\%$ from generation~0.
140	The 15\% threshold was selected post-hoc (robust band $[10\%, 22\%]$, zero false alarms; Appendix~\ref{app:intervention_sensitivity}).
141	The predictive trigger fires at generation~1 (one generation before a reactive distinct-1 baseline), reducing peak perplexity by 64\% ($56.99$ vs.\ $157.09$; Figure~\ref{fig:intervention}) in both Pythia-410M and 1.4B.
142	This single-setting ($\alpha{=}1.0$) demonstration is not rigorously evaluated (CUSUM comparison: Appendix~\ref{app:csmp}).
143	
144	\begin{figure}[t]
145	\centering
146	\includegraphics[width=0.6\columnwidth]{figures/fig_intervention.pdf}
147	\caption{Canary-triggered intervention (Pythia-410M, $\alpha{=}1.0$). Predictive cessation on entropy (generation~1) reduces peak perplexity by 64\% versus reactive triggering on distinct-1 (generation~2).}
148	\label{fig:intervention}
149	\end{figure}

\paragraph{Canary scoping.}
First-differencing scopes the canary claim precisely.
Canary$\to$diversity pairs retain unanimous FDR significance after first-differencing ($24/24 \to 24/24$ across 4~seeds at $\alpha{=}1.0$, 6 pairs per seed), while canary$\to$perplexity collapses entirely ($F \approx 0$, $p = 0.99$): the apparent perplexity association is a shared-trend artifact.
All canary claims are therefore scoped to diversity metrics only.
This scoping reflects a genuine temporal structure difference, not selective power loss from differencing: $|r|$ retention is ${\geq}95\%$ for both channels, but canary$\to$diversity correlations peak at lagged offsets (81\% at lag${<}0$, median${=}-1$) while canary$\to$perplexity correlations are contemporaneous (50\% at lag${=}0$), producing $20$--$28{\times}$ lower Granger $F$ for perplexity (Appendix~\ref{app:channel_effect_size}; perplexity $n{=}8$, limited sample).
At $\alpha{=}1.0$, all 24 canary$\to$diversity pairs (6 per seed $\times$ 4~seeds; mauve excluded) reach FDR significance in the forward direction with 0/24 reverse; directional asymmetry is robust across all WikiText conditions.

The canary mechanism also exhibits a blind spot: at $\alpha{=}0.10$, distinct-1 has already dropped by $39.6\%$, yet token entropy is indistinguishable from the null ($-5.3\%$ versus $-4.6{\pm}0.4\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.0$).
The gen-1 entropy deviation spans three orders of magnitude across the $\alpha$ range: $0.5\sigma$ at $\alpha{=}0.10$ to $60\sigma$ at $\alpha{=}0.75$ (relative to null variability), explaining why the blind zone persists despite increasing contamination.\footnote{Seed~43 at $\alpha{=}0.10$ shows 3/8 versus 0/8 for seed~42; no other sub-threshold level exhibits seed-dependent detection.}
Below $\alpha_c$ at $T{=}10$, diversity collapse proceeds without any detectable Granger-precedence signal in the canary metrics, though Gaussian MI remains positive (Appendix~\ref{app:mi_analysis}).

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\label{sec:discussion}

\paragraph{Scope of claims.}
Our Granger-precedence claim is scoped to temporal predictive improvement~\cite{granger1969investigating,shojaie2022granger}: bivariate tests cannot exclude confounders, and the cluster-adjusted FPR CI ($[1.2\%, 30.4\%]$; \S\ref{sec:limitations}) means true Type~I error may be non-negligible.
Five $\alpha{=}0.60$ cells are excluded from the boundary fit (sync-dip zone: 0/8 at $T{\leq}20$, dissolving to 5/8 at $T{=}25$); the remaining 15/15 match theory (LOO-CV MAE${=}0.037$).

\paragraph{When the canary fails.}
Four of fifteen cross-architecture conditions do not confirm forward detection (\S\ref{sec:generalization}), and each failure is interpretable.
SmolLM3-3B's non-monotonic entropy violates Proposition~\ref{thm:entropy_leads}'s monotonic-decline assumption, correctly predicting failure; GPT-2's precision sensitivity and Pythia-1.4B's seed dependence expose practical deployment constraints.
Phase-diagram structure is qualitatively preserved at 1.4B ($\alpha_c$ onset consistent, sync-dip absent); directional asymmetry is seed-sensitive above onset (s43 reverse 6/6 at $\alpha{\geq}0.60$; s42: 0/6; Appendix~\ref{app:scale_14b}).

\paragraph{Broader implications.}
Three findings carry practical weight.
First, the ${\geq}1$-generation entropy-diversity lag (14/15 experiments) provides an actionable early-warning window, and triggered cessation demonstrates that this window can be exploited (64\% perplexity reduction; \S\ref{sec:intervention}).
Second, the method-sensitivity results (3\% to 92\% FPR on identical data) are a cautionary finding for any collapse monitoring effort: conclusions are only as reliable as the statistical method used to reach them.
Third, the phase-diagram methodology itself transfers: the $\alpha_c(T)$ framework provides a template for characterizing detection boundaries in other iterative degradation settings.
Our contribution is this methodology, not frontier-scale applicability ($>$7B untested).

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related_work}

\paragraph{Model collapse and canary metrics.}
Iterative training collapse was formalized by \citet{shumailov2024curse} and \citet{alemohammad2024mad}, who showed that recursively replacing real data with model-generated text causes progressive tail erosion; \citet{dey2024breaking} demonstrated that data accumulation (rather than replacement) can mitigate collapse; \citet{schaeffer2025position} systematize eight distinct notions of ``collapse'' that this literature conflates.
Our operationalization---declining detection rate of Granger-precedence canary$\to$diversity links across generations---aligns most closely with Schaeffer et al.'s \emph{distributional shift} family (definitions~D4--D6 in their taxonomy), measuring how the generated distribution departs from the real-data baseline rather than tracking population risk or scaling-law exponents.
Theoretical analyses have sharpened these results: \citet{dohmatob2024tale} recast collapse as a change in scaling-law exponents, \citet{dohmatob2025strong} proved that collapse can occur even at vanishingly small synthetic fractions, \citet{seddik2025statistical} provide a statistical analysis of iterative contamination dynamics, and \citet{marchi2025challenging} challenge the universality of collapse under diverse training conditions.
Several works have proposed monitoring metrics: \citet{du2025scales} report ECE increases at 30\% contamination before accuracy drops, \citet{gambetta2024surplexity} introduces surplexity as a collapse detector, \citet{drayson2025detection} show that machine-generated text detection can prevent collapse, and \citet{li2025verification} propose verification-based mitigation.
\citet{shi2025closer} independently validate entropy as a collapse diagnostic in diffusion models ($r{=}0.91$ with generalization score), using it for diversity-aware sample selection.
\citet{du2026geometric} address a related but distinct phenomenon---mode collapse during generation---via geometric regulation of the representation trajectory; our work instead studies \emph{iterative training} collapse across generations.
We differ from prior monitoring work in four respects (comparison table: Appendix~\ref{app:method_comparison}): (i)~we compare an entire family of canary metrics; (ii)~we cross-validate across five statistical methods; (iii)~we map detectability as a function of contamination regime; and (iv)~we treat method-selection sensitivity itself as a primary finding.

\paragraph{Data mixing phase transitions.}
\citet{kazdan2025collapse} map the conditions under which synthetic data triggers collapse versus improves performance, \citet{gu2024cmr} establish a scaling law for critical mixture ratios in continual pre-training, and \citet{gu2025datamixing} show that data mixing can induce phase transitions in knowledge acquisition---a direct theoretical analogue to our detection threshold, where a critical mixing ratio separates qualitatively different detection regimes.

\paragraph{Critical transitions and lead-lag methodology.}
\citet{scheffer2009early} established that systems approaching tipping points exhibit generic early-warning signals (rising autocorrelation and variance); \citet{dakos2012methods} developed a practical toolkit for estimating such signals, while \citet{boettiger2012limits} quantified detection limits in short time series---directly relevant to iterative training where $T{=}5$--$20$.
Crucially, \citet{truong2026phase} prove that entropy collapse in iterative training is a first-order (discontinuous) phase transition, structurally ruling out critical-slowing-down (CSD) early-warning signals.
Our Granger-precedence approach circumvents this limitation by detecting temporal predictive improvement rather than variance/autocorrelation signatures, achieving ${\geq}5/8$ forward detection in 12 of 15 above-boundary cells (three sync-dip exceptions at $\alpha{=}0.60$ dissolve by $T{=}25$; \S\ref{sec:t20}).
The standard framework for testing temporal precedence is Granger causality~\cite{granger1969investigating}, with neural extensions for nonlinear settings~\citep{tank2021neural,marcinkevics2022neural,zeng2025kangci}; however, non-stationary series inflate rejection rates~\cite{granger1974spurious}, and the Toda--Yamamoto procedure~\cite{toda1995statistical} addresses this at reduced degrees of freedom severe in short series.
We use classical rather than neural Granger methods because $T{\leq}25$ provides insufficient observations for neural network parameter estimation.
These methods are largely absent from the model collapse literature.
Our analysis studies iterative from-scratch retraining; online or continual learning settings, where the model updates incrementally on streaming data, may exhibit different detection dynamics.

\paragraph{Analytical robustness.}
\citet{bell2022modeling} introduced multiverse analysis to ML, \citet{coretta2023multidimensional} demonstrated that 46 teams reached different conclusions on identical data, and \citet{kapoor2024reforms} synthesized these concerns into a consensus checklist.
Our work applies this perspective to model collapse: five methods across multiple contamination regimes produce conclusions ranging from universal significance to complete null.

\citet{shi2025closer} independently validate entropy as a collapse diagnostic in diffusion models ($r{=}0.91$ with generalization score), using it for diversity-aware sample selection.
\citet{du2026geometric} address a related but distinct phenomenon (mode collapse during generation) via geometric regulation of the representation trajectory; our work instead studies \emph{iterative training} collapse across generations.
We differ from prior monitoring work in four respects (comparison table: Appendix~\ref{app:method_comparison}): (i)~we compare an entire family of canary metrics; (ii)~we cross-validate across five statistical methods; (iii)~we map detectability as a function of contamination regime; and (iv)~we treat method-selection sensitivity itself as a primary finding.

\paragraph{Data mixing phase transitions.}
The observation that critical mixture ratios separate qualitatively different outcomes has precedent: \citet{kazdan2025collapse} map conditions under which synthetic data triggers collapse versus improves performance, and \citet{gu2024cmr} establish a scaling law for critical mixture ratios in continual pre-training.
\citet{gu2025datamixing} show that data mixing can induce phase transitions in knowledge acquisition, a direct theoretical analogue to our detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$.

\citet{scheffer2009early} established that systems approaching tipping points exhibit generic early-warning signals (rising autocorrelation and variance); \citet{dakos2012methods} developed a practical toolkit for estimating such signals, while \citet{boettiger2012limits} quantified detection limits in short time series---directly relevant to iterative training where $T{=}5$--$20$.
Crucially, \citet{truong2026phase} prove that entropy collapse in iterative training is a first-order (discontinuous) phase transition, structurally ruling out critical-slowing-down (CSD) early-warning signals.
Our Granger-precedence approach circumvents this limitation by detecting temporal predictive improvement rather than variance/autocorrelation signatures, achieving ${\geq}5/8$ forward detection in 12 of 15 above-boundary cells (three sync-dip exceptions at $\alpha{=}0.60$ dissolve by $T{=}25$; \S\ref{sec:t20}).

We use classical rather than neural Granger methods because $T{\leq}25$ provides insufficient observations for neural network parameter estimation.
These methods are largely absent from the model collapse literature.
Our analysis studies iterative from-scratch retraining; online or continual learning settings, where the model updates incrementally on streaming data, may exhibit different detection dynamics.

\paragraph{Analytical robustness.}
\citet{bell2022modeling} introduced multiverse analysis to ML, \citet{coretta2023multidimensional} demonstrated that 46 teams reached different conclusions on identical data, and \citet{kapoor2024reforms} synthesized these concerns into a consensus checklist.
Our work applies this perspective to model collapse: five methods across multiple contamination regimes produce conclusions ranging from universal significance to complete null.

\subsection{Detection Boundary Left-Shift}
\label{sec:t20}

Longer observation windows push the detection boundary to lower contamination levels: $\alpha_c(5){\geq}1.0$, $\alpha_c(10){=}0.487$, consistent with $T^{-2.08}$ power scaling (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
The $\alpha{=}0.45$ column provides the sharpest validation of this left-shift: undetectable at $T{\leq}10$ (0/8), it crosses into reliable detection at $T{=}15$ (6/8, dual-seed) and remains there at $T{=}20$ (5/8) and $T{=}25$ (6/8).
The systematic 2/8 gap reflects MAUVE floor saturation ($\mu{=}0.029$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
Cross-seed replication shows PermG within ${\pm}1$, though boundary cells exhibit sensitivity: $[0, 6]/8$ at ($T{=}10$, $\alpha{=}0.50$); $[0, 3]/8$ at ($T{=}20$, $\alpha{=}0.60$).
The $\alpha{=}0.60$ dip dissolves by $T{=}25$ ($5/8$), validating $\sqrt{T}$ power scaling; predict-then-verify yields 2/4 boundary predictions within CI (Appendix~\ref{app:t20_prediction_timeline}).

\subsection{Detection Boundary Left-Shift}
\label{sec:t20}

The detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$ decreases monotonically: $\alpha_c(5){\geq}1.0$, $\alpha_c(10){=}0.487$, consistent with $T^{-2.08}$ power scaling (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
The $\alpha{=}0.45$ column traces the sharpest validation: $0/8$ at $T{\leq}10$, $6/8$ at $T{=}15$ (dual-seed), $5/8$ at $T{=}20$, $6/8$ at $T{=}25$.
The systematic 2/8 gap reflects MAUVE floor saturation ($\mu{=}0.029$, SNR $4.68$ vs diversity $6.40$--$8.20$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
Cross-seed replication shows PermG within ${\pm}1$, though boundary cells exhibit sensitivity: $[0, 6]/8$ at ($T{=}10$, $\alpha{=}0.50$); $[0, 3]/8$ at ($T{=}20$, $\alpha{=}0.60$).
Minimum $T$ for 80\% power at $\alpha{=}0.50$ is approximately $T{=}30$ (extrapolated from simulation; Appendix~\ref{app:power_sim}).
The $\alpha{=}0.60$ dip dissolves by $T{=}25$ ($5/8$), validating $\sqrt{T}$ power scaling; predict-then-verify (commit \texttt{bad72cc}) yields 2/4 boundary predictions within CI (Appendix~\ref{app:t20_prediction_timeline}).

\subsection{Detection Boundary Left-Shift}
\label{sec:t20}

Longer observation windows push the detection boundary to lower contamination levels: $\alpha_c(5){\geq}1.0$, $\alpha_c(10){=}0.487$, consistent with $T^{-2.08}$ power scaling (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
The $\alpha{=}0.45$ column provides the sharpest validation of this left-shift: undetectable at $T{\leq}10$ (0/8), it crosses into reliable detection at $T{=}15$ (6/8, dual-seed) and remains there at $T{=}20$ (5/8) and $T{=}25$ (6/8).
The systematic 2/8 gap reflects MAUVE floor saturation ($\mu{=}0.029$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
Cross-seed replication shows PermG within ${\pm}1$, though boundary cells exhibit sensitivity: $[0, 6]/8$ at ($T{=}10$, $\alpha{=}0.50$); $[0, 3]/8$ at ($T{=}20$, $\alpha{=}0.60$).
The $\alpha{=}0.60$ dip dissolves by $T{=}25$ ($5/8$), validating $\sqrt{T}$ power scaling; predict-then-verify yields 2/4 boundary predictions within CI (Appendix~\ref{app:t20_prediction_timeline}).

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

When language models train iteratively on their own output, the training distribution progressively loses its tail modes, a phenomenon termed model collapse~\cite{shumailov2024curse,alemohammad2024mad}.
Lexical diversity narrows, calibration deteriorates, and each generation inherits the systematic biases of its predecessors.
As machine-generated text becomes prevalent on the web, such feedback loops pose a growing risk to production training pipelines.
By the time standard quality metrics register degradation, the underlying distribution may have already shifted irreversibly.

This threat motivates a fundamental question: \emph{what does the detectability landscape of model collapse look like?}
At what contamination level does statistical detection become possible, how does this boundary depend on observation length, and what structure does the landscape exhibit?
These questions are nontrivial because iterative training produces short, noisy time series (often fewer than 15 points), where detection power drops sharply~\cite{boettiger2012limits}. Moreover, model collapse is a first-order transition~\cite{truong2026phase}, structurally ruling out the critical-slowing-down early-warning signals that ecologists rely on~\cite{scheffer2009early} (\S\ref{sec:related_work}).

We map this landscape on Pythia-410M~\cite{biderman2023pythia} across 13 contamination levels with multi-seed replication, and find that it has rich structure (Figure~\ref{fig:regime_map}).
Rather than a smooth degradation curve, the landscape contains blind zones where collapse proceeds undetected, a sharp onset where detection jumps from null to reliable within a 2-percentage-point interval, a non-monotonic dip where detection temporarily fails, and a power-law detection boundary $\alpha_c(T) \propto T^{-2.08}$.
Cross-architecture validation across five families (345M--6.9B) confirms that this structure generalizes when entropy-diversity coupling is preserved.
A second finding is equally consequential: five statistical methods applied to identical data yield null-control false-positive rates from 3\% to 92\%, demonstrating that the landscape one observes depends critically on the method used to probe it.
Granger precedence establishes temporal predictive improvement, not true causality~\cite{shojaie2022granger}; our canary claim is scoped to diversity metrics (distinct-$n$~\cite{li2016diversity}).

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Detectability landscape characterization} (\S\ref{sec:regime}--\ref{sec:intervention}).
    PermG establishes a detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$ (Pythia-410M primary; cross-architecture at $\alpha{=}1.0$) following a power law in observation length (Eq.~\ref{eq:alpha-c-theory}; leave-one-$T$-out CV: MAE${=}0.037$, 15/15 cells within CI).
    Any nonzero contamination produces signal, but sub-linear growth makes detection a function of $T$.
    A proof-of-concept intervention (N${=}2$ seeds, $\alpha{=}1.0$, Pythia-410M) demonstrates that canary-triggered cessation can reduce peak perplexity by 64\%.

    \item \textbf{Formal design rationale for canary metric selection} (\S\ref{sec:cascade}).
    Under mode amplification, entropy responds before diversity by ${\geq}1$ generation (Design Principles~\ref{thm:entropy_leads}--\ref{prop:div_lag}), confirmed in 14/15 experiments ($\alpha \geq 0.30$; GPT-2-medium s43 bidirectional).

    \item \textbf{Method sensitivity as a primary finding} (\S\ref{sec:mmct}--\ref{sec:dose_response}).
    Five detection methods yield null-control FPR from 3\% to 92\%; the same Granger test shifts from 0/8 to 6/8 within a 2-percentage-point interval, motivating method sensitivity as a first-order concern.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.55\textwidth]{figures/fig_phase_diagram.pdf}
\caption{Detection phase diagram (Pythia-410M, fp32, PermG direction-checked). Each cell shows the number of FDR-significant canary$\to$diversity pairs (of~8) at a given contamination strength~$\alpha$ and observation window~$T$. The dashed curve is the theoretical detection boundary $\alpha_c(T) \propto T^{-\gamma}$ with $\gamma{=}2.08$, fitted (Eq.~\ref{eq:alpha-c-theory}). Diamond markers ($\diamond$) flag the synchronous dip at $\alpha{=}0.60$ (0/8 at $T{\leq}20$); the star ($\star$) marks its dissolution at $T{=}25$ (5/8), validating $\sqrt{T}$ power scaling.}
\label{fig:regime_map}
\end{figure*}

3	description: 顶会级别论文写作风格规范——章节写法（Abstract/Intro/Related Work）、去 AI 风格、视觉密度、叙事哲学。Paper Agent 和 Worker 写论文章节时必须加载。
4	allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep]
5	scope: global

7	priority: 9

9	  - writing

14	  - agent

16	  - paper_agent
17	---
18	
19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	### 6.5 页面节奏
214	
215	好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：
216	
217	- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
218	- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
219	- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
220	- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
221	- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）
222	
223	### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范
224	
225	**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
226	- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
227	- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
228	- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
229	- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
230	- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）
231	
232	**宽度决策树**：
233	- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
234	- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
235	- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix
236	
237	---
238	
239	## 七、投稿前通用准备
240	
241	### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）
242	
243	- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
244	- **不要用**：
245	  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
246	  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
247	  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
248	- 风险：
249	  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
250	  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
251	  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
252	- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
253	- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致
254	
255	### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对
256	
257	- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
258	- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
259	- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
260	- 行号开启（review 版常需）
261	- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件
262	
263	### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程
264	
265	提交前必须逐一检查：
266	1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
267	2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
268	3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
269	4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
270	5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
271	6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
272	7. 所有专有名词有定义
273	8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
274	9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
275	10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础
276

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

### 3.3 禁忌

- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

### 4.2 结构要求

- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash

  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```

- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用

2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写

---

- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比

- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开

- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）

---

## 七、投稿前通用准备

### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）

- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
- **不要用**：
  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
- 风险：
  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致

### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对

- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
- 行号开启（review 版常需）
- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件

### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程

提交前必须逐一检查：
1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
7. 所有专有名词有定义
8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

\begin{abstract}
When language models train on their own output, distributional quality degrades well before standard metrics register collapse.
Detecting this degradation early is difficult: the time series are short ($T{\leq}25$ generations), the signal is sub-linear in contamination fraction, and, as we show, the choice of statistical test can shift conclusions from universal detection to complete null.
We characterize the detectability landscape of iterative model collapse, primarily on Pythia-410M across 13 contamination levels with cross-architecture validation on five families (Pythia, GPT-2, OPT, Qwen, SmolLM3; 345M--6.9B); the full $(\alpha, T)$ grid is specific to Pythia-410M, with cross-architecture tests at $\alpha{=}1.0$.
Using permutation Granger causality\footnote{Granger precedence establishes temporal predictive improvement, not true causation~\cite{shojaie2022granger}.} (PermG), we identify a detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$ that follows a power law in observation length (leave-one-$T$-out CV: MAE${=}0.037$, 15/15 cells within CI), structured into four regimes: a blind zone, a sharp onset, a non-monotonic dip, and a reliable detection region.
Five statistical methods applied to identical data yield null-control false positive rates from 3\% to 92\%, with the best directional method (PermG) at 11\%, exposing method sensitivity as a primary concern rather than a robustness footnote.
Entropy Granger-precedes diversity collapse by ${\geq}1$ generation (14/15 experiments), providing a canary signal whose triggered cessation reduces peak perplexity by 64\% in a proof-of-concept intervention.
\end{abstract}

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	When language models train iteratively on their own output, the training distribution progressively loses its tail modes, a phenomenon termed model collapse~\cite{shumailov2024curse,alemohammad2024mad}.
5	Lexical diversity narrows, calibration deteriorates, and each generation inherits the systematic biases of its predecessors.
6	As machine-generated text becomes prevalent on the web, such feedback loops pose a growing risk to production training pipelines.
7	By the time standard quality metrics register degradation, the underlying distribution may have already shifted irreversibly.
8	
9	This threat motivates a fundamental question: \emph{what does the detectability landscape of model collapse look like?}
10	At what contamination level does statistical detection become possible, how does this boundary depend on observation length, and what structure does the landscape exhibit?
11	These questions are nontrivial because iterative training produces short, noisy time series (often fewer than 15 points), where detection power drops sharply~\cite{boettiger2012limits}. Moreover, model collapse is a first-order transition~\cite{truong2026phase}, structurally ruling out the critical-slowing-down early-warning signals that ecologists rely on~\cite{scheffer2009early} (\S\ref{sec:related_work}).
12	
13	We map this landscape on Pythia-410M~\cite{biderman2023pythia} across 13 contamination levels with multi-seed replication, and find that it has rich structure (Figure~\ref{fig:regime_map}).
14	Rather than a smooth degradation curve, the landscape contains blind zones where collapse proceeds undetected, a sharp onset where detection jumps from null to reliable within a 2-percentage-point interval, a non-monotonic dip where detection temporarily fails, and a power-law detection boundary $\alpha_c(T) \propto T^{-2.08}$.
15	Cross-architecture validation across five families (345M--6.9B) confirms that this structure generalizes when entropy-diversity coupling is preserved.
16	A second finding is equally consequential: five statistical methods applied to identical data yield null-control false-positive rates from 3\% to 92\%, demonstrating that the landscape one observes depends critically on the method used to probe it.
17	Granger precedence establishes temporal predictive improvement, not true causality~\cite{shojaie2022granger}; our canary claim is scoped to diversity metrics (distinct-$n$~\cite{li2016diversity}).
18	
19	Our contributions are:
20	\begin{enumerate}
21	    \item \textbf{Detectability landscape characterization} (\S\ref{sec:regime}--\ref{sec:intervention}).
22	    PermG establishes a detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$ (Pythia-410M primary; cross-architecture at $\alpha{=}1.0$) following a power law in observation length (Eq.~\ref{eq:alpha-c-theory}; leave-one-$T$-out CV: MAE${=}0.037$, 15/15 cells within CI).
23	    Any nonzero contamination produces signal, but sub-linear growth makes detection a function of $T$.
24	    A proof-of-concept intervention (N${=}2$ seeds, $\alpha{=}1.0$, Pythia-410M) demonstrates that canary-triggered cessation can reduce peak perplexity by 64\%.
25	
26	    \item \textbf{Formal design rationale for canary metric selection} (\S\ref{sec:cascade}).
27	    Under mode amplification, entropy responds before diversity by ${\geq}1$ generation (Design Principles~\ref{thm:entropy_leads}--\ref{prop:div_lag}), confirmed in 14/15 experiments ($\alpha \geq 0.30$; GPT-2-medium s43 bidirectional).
28	
29	    \item \textbf{Method sensitivity as a primary finding} (\S\ref{sec:mmct}--\ref{sec:dose_response}).
30	    Five detection methods yield null-control FPR from 3\% to 92\%; the same Granger test shifts from 0/8 to 6/8 within a 2-percentage-point interval, motivating method sensitivity as a first-order concern.
31	\end{enumerate}
32	
33	\begin{figure*}[t]
34	\centering
35	\includegraphics[width=0.55\textwidth]{figures/fig_phase_diagram.pdf}
36	\caption{Detection phase diagram (Pythia-410M, fp32, PermG direction-checked). \section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

When language models train iteratively on their own output, the training distribution progressively loses its tail modes, a phenomenon termed model collapse~\cite{shumailov2024curse,alemohammad2024mad}.
Lexical diversity narrows, calibration deteriorates, and each generation inherits the systematic biases of its predecessors.
As machine-generated text becomes prevalent on the web, such feedback loops pose a growing risk to production training pipelines.
By the time standard quality metrics register degradation, the underlying distribution may have already shifted irreversibly.

This threat motivates a fundamental question: \emph{what does the detectability landscape of model collapse look like?}
At what contamination level does statistical detection become possible, how does this boundary depend on observation length, and what structure does the landscape exhibit?
These questions are nontrivial because iterative training produces short, noisy time series (often fewer than 15 points), where detection power drops sharply~\cite{boettiger2012limits}. Moreover, model collapse is a first-order transition~\cite{truong2026phase}, structurally ruling out the critical-slowing-down early-warning signals that ecologists rely on~\cite{scheffer2009early} (\S\ref{sec:related_work}).

We map this landscape on Pythia-410M~\cite{biderman2023pythia} across 13 contamination levels with multi-seed replication, and find that it has rich structure (Figure~\ref{fig:regime_map}).
Rather than a smooth degradation curve, the landscape contains blind zones where collapse proceeds undetected, a sharp onset where detection jumps from null to reliable within a 2-percentage-point interval, a non-monotonic dip where detection temporarily fails, and a power-law detection boundary $\alpha_c(T) \propto T^{-2.08}$.
Cross-architecture validation across five families (345M--6.9B) confirms that this structure generalizes when entropy-diversity coupling is preserved.
A second finding is equally consequential: five statistical methods applied to identical data yield null-control false-positive rates from 3\% to 92\%, demonstrating that the landscape one observes depends critically on the method used to probe it.
Granger precedence establishes temporal predictive improvement, not true causality~\cite{shojaie2022granger}; our canary claim is scoped to diversity metrics (distinct-$n$~\cite{li2016diversity}).

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Detectability landscape characterization} (\S\ref{sec:regime}--\ref{sec:intervention}).
    PermG establishes a detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$ (Pythia-410M primary; cross-architecture at $\alpha{=}1.0$) following a power law in observation length (Eq.~\ref{eq:alpha-c-theory}; leave-one-$T$-out CV: MAE${=}0.037$, 15/15 cells within CI).
    Any nonzero contamination produces signal, but sub-linear growth makes detection a function of $T$.
    A proof-of-concept intervention (N${=}2$ seeds, $\alpha{=}1.0$, Pythia-410M) demonstrates that canary-triggered cessation can reduce peak perplexity by 64\%.

    \item \textbf{Formal design rationale for canary metric selection} (\S\ref{sec:cascade}).
    Under mode amplification, entropy responds before diversity by ${\geq}1$ generation (Design Principles~\ref{thm:entropy_leads}--\ref{prop:div_lag}), confirmed in 14/15 experiments ($\alpha \geq 0.30$; GPT-2-medium s43 bidirectional).

    \item \textbf{Method sensitivity as a primary finding} (\S\ref{sec:mmct}--\ref{sec:dose_response}).
    Five detection methods yield null-control FPR from 3\% to 92\%; the same Granger test shifts from 0/8 to 6/8 within a 2-percentage-point interval, motivating method sensitivity as a first-order concern.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.55\textwidth]{figures/fig_phase_diagram.pdf}
\caption{Detection phase diagram (Pythia-410M, fp32, PermG direction-checked). Each cell shows the number of FDR-significant canary$\to$diversity pairs (of~8) at a given contamination strength~$\alpha$ and observation window~$T$. The dashed curve is the theoretical detection boundary $\alpha_c(T) \propto T^{-\gamma}$ with $\gamma{=}2.08$, fitted (Eq.~\ref{eq:alpha-c-theory}). Diamond markers ($\diamond$) flag the synchronous dip at $\alpha{=}0.60$ (0/8 at $T{\leq}20$); the star ($\star$) marks its dissolution at $T{=}25$ (5/8), validating $\sqrt{T}$ power scaling.}
\label{fig:regime_map}
\end{figure*}

    On Pythia-410M (cross-architecture at $\alpha{=}1.0$), PermG identifies a power-law detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$ (Eq.~\ref{eq:alpha-c-theory}; LOO-CV: MAE${=}0.037$, 15/15 within CI): any nonzero contamination produces signal, but sub-linear growth makes detection a function of $T$.
    Canary-triggered cessation reduces peak perplexity by 64\% in a proof-of-concept intervention.

    \item \textbf{We establish a formal design rationale for canary metric selection} (\S\ref{sec:cascade}).
    Under mode amplification, entropy responds before diversity by ${\geq}1$ generation (Design Principles~\ref{thm:entropy_leads}--\ref{prop:div_lag}), confirmed in 14/15 experiments ($\alpha \geq 0.30$; GPT-2-medium s43 bidirectional).

    \item \textbf{We document method sensitivity as a primary finding} (\S\ref{sec:mmct}--\ref{sec:dose_response}).
    Five methods yield null-control FPR from 3\% to 92\%; the same Granger test shifts from 0/8 to 6/8 within 2 percentage points, demonstrating that the landscape one observes depends on the method used to probe it.
